bullets.title: MU Options Volume Hits $1.5B, Exceeding SPY+QQQ Combined—Stock Loses $94B Market Cap
bullets.body: Micron options traded ~$1.5B in notional premium, exceeding SPY and QQQ (~$1B each) combined—described as 'insane' by SpotGamma. MU simultaneously shed $94B in market cap, a move exceeding 1 standard deviation for top-20 stocks, raising questions about broader semiconductor sector health.

bullets.title: AVGO Soft Guidance Sparks AI-Sector Pre-Market Selloff
bullets.body: Stocks fell in pre-market after Broadcom issued soft guidance Wednesday night, triggering weakness across AI-related names. Strong May jobs data compounded pressure by fueling 'higher for longer' rate fears; Brent crude slipped to $95/bbl and Bitcoin dropped 1.5% to $62.6K.

bullets.title: JPMorgan Upgrades TSLA to Neutral, Raises PT to $475 from $145 on Robotics/AI Thesis
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded Tesla from Underweight to Neutral and dramatically raised its price target to $475 from $145, shifting the thesis away from near-term EV earnings toward autonomous driving, robotics, AI, and software optionality. Multiple fintwit accounts flagged the magnitude of the PT raise as notable.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang Certifies Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix as HBM4 Suppliers
bullets.body: Jensen Huang certified all three major HBM suppliers—Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix—as qualified for HBM4 memory in Nvidia's next-generation chips, a positive supply-chain signal for MU. Separately, SK Hynix fell nearly 10% on KOSPI in what market commentators flagged as a potential 'first crack' in crowded semiconductor trades.

bullets.title: EQIX: REITweek Transcript Incrementally Positive but Equity Setup Deteriorated Post-Rerating
bullets.body: Fintwit analyst notes the REITweek transcript is 'incrementally supportive' for Equinix's long-term quality-compounder thesis, but warns the equity setup is 'no longer clean' after a material rerating. Key risks flagged include grid interconnection delays, equipment bottlenecks, community resistance, water constraints, and regulatory scrutiny.

bullets.title: NVDA Uses AMD EPYC (Not Intel) in Switch Trays—Small but Telling Supply Win for AMD
bullets.body: A noted tech analyst flagged that NVIDIA uses AMD EPYC processors in its switch trays rather than Intel hardware, a detail underscoring AMD's competitive positioning in data center infrastructure adjacent to Nvidia's buildout.

bullets.title: AAPL WWDC Monday: Analyst Expects AI Announcements to Be Key Focus
bullets.body: An analyst flagged Apple's WWDC event Monday in Cupertino as a major catalyst, planning to discuss AI expectations on CNBC Closing Bell at 3pm. Apple noted as having LTA negotiating advantages vs. competitors, though its scale prevents large-scale stockpiling without moving markets.

bullets.title: Foxconn May Revenue +39.6% YoY to $27.3B—Q2 Tracking 'Well Above' Prior Guidance on AI Servers
bullets.body: Foxconn reported May revenue of NT$859.4B ($27.3B), up 39.6% YoY and the company's 3rd best month ever, driven by AI server assembly and iPhone production. Management said Q2 is tracking 'well above previously anticipated significant growth'—a positive read-through for AI infrastructure spending.

bullets.title: Citi Bear Market Checklist at 10/18: Global Stocks at Frothiest Since 2008
bullets.body: Citi's Bear Market Checklist has reached 10 out of 18 risk flags globally, with the firm warning global stocks are at their frothiest valuation levels since the 2008 financial crisis. AI-driven spending, elevated bullish sentiment, and a surge in IPO activity are cited as key contributors.

bullets.title: BCA Warns Fed Risks Inflating AI-Fueled Stock Bubble
bullets.body: BCA Research warns the Federal Reserve is underestimating AI-driven inflation—particularly rising electricity and memory chip costs—and is keeping rates too low, risking the inflation of a stock bubble. The warning compounds existing market froth concerns flagged by Citi.

bullets.title: Anthropic Urges Global Pause in AI Development as Models Near Self-Improvement Capability
bullets.body: Anthropic has publicly called for a global pause in AI development, citing that artificial intelligence models are approaching the capability to self-improve without human intervention. This is a significant policy signal from one of the leading frontier AI labs.

bullets.title: Risk-On Positioning Back to Pre-Pandemic Highs Despite Froth Warnings
bullets.body: Market risk-on positioning metrics have rebounded to pre-pandemic highs, signaling renewed investor appetite for growth and higher-beta assets—a notable contrast to simultaneous warnings from Citi and BCA about stretched valuations.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz Risk Mispriced for 90 Days; Rosneft Warns $150/bbl Oil if Closed
bullets.body: Jim Bianco argues markets have been consistently wrong about Strait of Hormuz risk for 90 days by treating disruption as temporary. Separately, Rosneft CEO Sechin warned no country can replace Middle East oil supply and prices could hit $150/bbl if the strait closes. Iran also fired warning shots at U.S. Navy destroyers in the Gulf of Oman, escalating tensions.

bullets.title: Drewry Container Shipping Index Jumps 23% W/W to $3,433; NY Fed Supply Chain Gauge Elevated
bullets.body: The Drewry World Container Index surged 23% over the past week to $3,433 per 40-foot container, while the NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index held elevated at 1.77 in May. Commentators cited Iran tensions as a contributing factor to ongoing supply chain stress and transport cost inflation.

bullets.title: BofA: Jobs/CPI Alignment at 4.2% Would Be Only 7th Such Instance Since 1960
bullets.body: Michael Hartnett at BofA notes that if May unemployment prints at or below 4.2%—in line with expected CPI next week—it would mark only the 7th such alignment since 1960, with prior instances in 1966, 1973, 1990, and 2000. The pattern flags a historically unusual macro configuration.

bullets.title: Eurozone Q1 GDP Contracts 0.2% QoQ, Misses 0.1% Estimate; YoY Slows to 0.3%
bullets.body: Eurozone Q1 GDP came in at -0.2% QoQ vs. the 0.1% consensus estimate, and just 0.3% YoY versus 0.8% expected—a significant deceleration signaling European economic weakness that could weigh on global risk sentiment.

bullets.title: Major Banks Building Tokenized Deposit Network via The Clearing House to Compete with Crypto
bullets.body: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, and Wells Fargo are building a tokenized deposit network operated by The Clearing House, designed to offer crypto-speed 24/7 settlement while keeping deposits within the traditional banking system.

bullets.title: Congress Pushing 25% Tax Credit for Domestic PCB Makers; Sanmina Named as Beneficiary
bullets.body: U.S. Congress is advancing the Protecting Circuit Boards and Substrates Act, which would offer a 25% tax credit to companies choosing U.S.-made PCBs and allocate $3B in subsidies to domestic manufacturers. Sanmina is specifically cited as positioned to benefit from the legislation.

bullets.title: Japan FX Intervention Risk Could Trigger US Treasury Sales—Global Macro Spillover Watch
bullets.body: A macro commentator flags that Japan's massive foreign securities holdings create spillover risk globally: FX intervention by Japan can force US Treasury sales, with implications for US rates and broader markets—a watch item given ongoing yen dynamics.

bullets.title: 1Q Unit Labor Costs Revised Down to +1.8%; Productivity Also Trimmed to +0.3%
bullets.body: Q1 unit labor costs were revised down to +1.8% from the initial +2.3% print, while productivity growth was trimmed to +0.3% from +0.8%—a modestly disinflationary revision that could influence Fed messaging, though weak productivity is a structural concern.
